rack_open_2520.body:
A few independent, behavior-preserving performance improvements, one commit each:

- `Request#ssl?` called `#scheme`, which can parse the forwarded headers, up to twice. `#forwarded_scheme` also looked up the same header twice.
- `Request::AUTHORITY` matched the host part lazily. The address character class does not include `:`, so a greedy match cannot consume the port separator and gives the same result, without backtracking at every character.
- `CommonLogger` ran `gsub!(/[^[:print:]]/)` on every log line. It is now skipped when the line is ASCII-only and contains no `\x00`-`\x1f` or `\x7f` (for ASCII, these are exactly the characters `[^[:print:]]` matches), which `String#ascii_only?` and `String#count` check much faster.
- `Response` created a `method(:append)` object for every response. It now uses `nil` as the default writer and calls `#append` directly.
- The multipart parser compiled its MIME head regexp, which does not depend on the boundary, for every request. It is now a constant, and the body regexps are built from a shared source string instead of interpolating one `Regexp` into another.

### Measurements

Ruby 3.4.10 with YJIT, x86_64 Linux. Instructions are user-space instructions per call from `perf stat`, taking the difference between 2,000 and 12,000 iterations so startup is excluded. Allocations are from `GC.stat(:total_allocated_objects)`.

| | instructions | allocations |
|---|---|---|
| `Request` accessors (`get?`, `path`, `fullpath`, `host`, `port`, `scheme`, `ssl?`, `url`, `ip`, `xhr?`, `content_type`, `media_type`) | 107.6k → 88.1k (−18%) | 55 → 40 |
| GET through `MethodOverride`, `Runtime`, `CommonLogger`, `ShowExceptions`, `ContentLength`, `Head`, `ConditionalGet`, `ETag`, `TempfileReaper` | 130.0k → 99.5k (−23%) | 38 → 37 |
| `Request#POST` with a 3-part multipart body (one 2 KB file) | 535.8k → 468.3k (−13%) | 215 → 193 |
| `Response` with a cookie and two `write` calls, then `finish` and iterating the body | 32.1k → 30.0k (−7%) | 19 → 18 |

How much of this shows up end to end depends on the app. With puma (one thread) and `ab -k`, a plain Rack app using `CommonLogger` uses about 4% fewer instructions per GET request. For the Sinatra 4.2, Roda and Rails 8.1 apps I tested, which do not use `CommonLogger`, the difference was within 1%.

### Equivalence

In addition to the test suite:

- For 30,000 random environments (random `HTTP_HOST`/`SERVER_NAME` including IPv6, ports and invalid characters, `HTTPS`, `X-Forwarded-*` and `Forwarded` headers), the results of `scheme`, `ssl?`, `authority`, `host`, `hostname`, `port`, `host_with_port`, `base_url`, `url`, `forwarded_authority` and `forwarded_port`, or the raised exception classes, were identical to the current implementation.
- For 5,000 random multipart bodies (random boundaries, nested names, file parts, embedded boundary-like data, truncated bodies and large parts), the parsed params, including file contents, or the raised exception classes, were identical.
rack_open_2520.title: Performance improvements in Request, CommonLogger, Response and the multipart parser
